IHNA Online Student portal redesign: before and after

    A clearer, calmer student portal

    What we changed in the IHNA Online student portal, and why, from the dashboard down to a single lesson.

    Shown with CHC33021 Certificate III in Individual Support (Ageing and Disability) and the unit CHCDIV001 Work with diverse people.

    What we set out to fix

    The current portal has everything a student needs, but it’s hard to tell what to do next. Four problems stood out in the screenshots.

    No clear next step

    The dashboard shows stats, cards and a chart, but no way to pick up the lesson you were on.

    Fixed by “Continue learning”

    A crowded sidebar

    27 staff names sit under the menu on every page, so the sidebar runs nearly three times the length of its menu.

    Fixed by a “Your support team” card

    Long scrolling lessons

    Every item in a chapter is stacked on one page. The learning activities page holds six videos and all their questions.

    Fixed by one item at a time

    Progress that’s hard to read

    All 10 chapters say “In Progress” and the unit shows 0%, so students can’t see what’s done and what’s left.

    Fixed by item and chapter progress

    Getting back to your lesson

    The most common reason to log in is to carry on learning. We made that the first thing on the dashboard.

    1 clickinstead of 3 clicks and a scroll

    BeforeDashboard to the next lesson item

    1. 1Open My Units›
    2. 2Continue on CHCDIV001›
    3. 3Pick a chapter card›
    4. +Scroll to find the item

    AfterDashboard to the next lesson item

    1. 1Resume lesson opens the next item directly

    The path through My units and the chapter list is still there for students who want to choose something else.

    Dashboard

    • “Continue learning” panel at the topOpens the next item in one click, with progress for the current chapter.
    • Four to-do cards became one list“Needs your attention” is easier to scan, with each action button lined up on the right.
    • Six stat boxes and a trend chart became one cardThe 8-week chart showed two flat lines across a full screen. The key numbers now sit together.
    • 16 unit cards became the 4 in progressThe full list is one click away in My units.
    BeforeAfter

    Drag the handle to compare

    Navigation and your support team

    • Staff names moved out of the sidebar27 trainers, coordinators and support officers now sit in one “Your support team” card on the dashboard, with the coordinator first.
    • Links grouped into Learn, Connect and My recordsStudents see the learning links first and everything fits without scrolling.
    • Plain-language names“SBT (Simulation Based Training)” became “Simulation training”, “My Chats” became “Messages”, and Feedback Center and Complaints were combined.

    Both at the same scale. Scroll to see the old sidebar run nearly twice as long.

    My units

    • Filters with counts, and searchIn progress, Not started, Credit transfer and Complete help students find what’s left in a list of 16.
    • A status label on every unitCredit transfer units show their status instead of an empty action, so nobody wonders why there’s no button.
    • Module progress as a bar“6 of 10” plus a bar reads faster than two small fractions.
    BeforeAfter

    Drag the handle to compare

    Unit chapters

    • Chapters grouped by session along a pathEach session shows its lesson and its learning activities together, in the order students take them.
    • Real progress on every chapter“1 of 4 done” replaces ten identical “In Progress” labels, and the header counts items, not just finished chapters.
    • Assessments and resources beside the chaptersThe learner guide, online link and study tools are easy to find without opening chapters 9 and 10.
    BeforeAfter

    Drag the handle to compare

    The lesson player

    • One item at a time, in a large playerInstead of four items stacked on one long page, students focus on a single video, module, lecture or tutorial.
    • The sidebar shows only this unit’s chaptersEach chapter has its own progress, and the current one opens to show its items. My units and All chapters sit at the top.
    • Previous, Next and Mark as completeNext names the item that comes up and carries on into the next chapter. Marking complete moves you on.
    BeforeAfter

    Also seen: the Session 2 introduction video shows a privacy-settings message instead of playing. That needs fixing in the video’s embed settings whichever design is used.

    Full screen and fewer distractions

    Before, the portal’s header, sidebar and the rest of the chapter stayed on screen around every video. Now students can clear them away.

    • Full screenHides everything but the player and Previous, Mark as complete and Next.
    • Hide menuGives the player the full width while keeping the top bar.
    • Keyboard shortcuts← and → move between items, F toggles full screen and M shows or hides the menu.

    After: full screen mode

    Learning activities and quizzes

    • Each video is followed by its own quiz slideSame order as before, but students meet one video or one quiz at a time instead of the whole page at once.
    • One question at a time, with feedback“Check answer” shows the right option and a short explanation, so the quiz teaches as well as tests.
    • A score at the end, and try againFinishing a quiz ticks it off in the chapter menu.

    The quiz questions in the prototype are drafts. The real question bank goes in before launch.

    Before: one long page (scroll it)

    After: one item at a time

    Built for every learner, on any screen

    • A typeface made for legibilityAtkinson Hyperlegible Next was designed for low-vision readers, with letters that are hard to mix up.
    • Readable contrast and large touch targetsText meets the 4.5:1 contrast guideline and buttons are at least 44 px tall.
    • Keyboard and screen reader supportReal buttons and links, labelled icons, focus outlines and announcements when the lesson changes.
    • Phone layouts and dark modeOn phones the menu becomes a button and the chapter list slides over the lesson. The portal follows the device’s light or dark setting.

    Summary of changes

    Every change aims at the same thing: show students where they are and what to do next.

    AreaBeforeAfterWhy
    DashboardStats, cards, unit grid and an 8-week chartContinue learning, one to-do list, one progress cardOne click back into learning
    NavigationMenu plus 27 staff names in the sidebarGrouped menu; staff in a support team cardShorter, easier to scan
    My unitsOne long list in two clustersFilters, search and a status per unitFind what’s left quickly
    Unit chapters10 cards all marked “In Progress”, unit at 0%Sessions on a path with real progressSee what’s done and what’s next
    LessonFour items stacked on one pageOne item at a time with a chapter menuLess scrolling, more focus
    ControlsPage scrolling and a Mark as Complete buttonPrevious, Next, Mark as complete, Hide menu, Full screenMove through a unit without losing your place
    ActivitiesSix videos and their questions on one pageVideo, then its quiz, one question at a timeImmediate feedback, clearer progress
    AccessDesktop layoutPhone layouts, dark mode, keyboard and screen reader supportWorks for every learner, on any screen

    Next steps

    The prototype covers one path through one unit. These steps take it to launch.

    1. Test with a handful of studentsAsk five to eight learners to resume a lesson, find a unit and finish a quiz, and watch where they hesitate.
    2. Load the real contentSwap in the actual quiz questions, connect the videos and interactive modules, and fix the Session 2 video’s embed settings.
    3. Design the remaining pagesTimetable, Assessments, Placement and the other links in the same style.
    4. Hand over to developmentShare the prototype, colours, type and components with the LMS team, and agree how progress is tracked.
